hints.title: Insertion Leaf Placement Obstacle
hints.text: The search tree invariant must hold after insertion. When searching for the value's location, what should happen when a null branch is reached?

hints.title: Leaf Attachment Invariant
hints.text: Follow search tree comparisons downward until reaching a null pointer where the new value belongs as a leaf node.

hints.title: Iterative Leaf Insertion Procedure
hints.text: If root is null, return a new node with val. Otherwise, traverse iteratively: if val < curr.val, move left if curr.left exists, else attach new node to curr.left and return root. If val > curr.val, move right if curr.right exists, else attach new node to curr.right and return root.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: H: height of BST (log N balanced, N worst-case)
complexity.notes: Iterative descent to the leaf attachment location with O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Restructuring the entire tree during insertion adds unnecessary O(N) complexity.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Iterative search uses zero extra call-stack memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Inserting the new key as a leaf without modifying existing parent-child bonds.
